_doc: What the bot may do with a vault, per venue. vault/policy.mjs compiles a venue's rules
plus 'common' and 'payout' into policies on chain, as many as their size needs (one
settings transaction carries one policy, so each must fit a transaction).
Each pin names an account of the instruction by position and the role it must play:
pool          one of the pools the owners approved for this vault
vault         the vault itself
vaultToken    an account whose token-owner field is the vault. Enough where the
instruction moves tokens into it: the token program rejects anything
that is not a real token account
vaultWsol     the same, and owned by the SPL Token program: for a plain SOL transfer,
which no token program checks
vaultOrPayer  the vault, or the bot's payer (rent the payer paid goes back to it)
payout        a token account of a payout wallet (profit wallet, fee wallet)
none          the venue program itself: the placeholder for an empty optional account
Only accounts money can flow to are pinned, plus the pool. The vault's own signature
(the wallet of an associated token account is pinned the same way: index 2 = vault)
needs no pin: no other account can sign as the vault. An instruction not listed here
cannot run through the vault. Discriminators are the venue programs' own
(Anchor: sha256('global:<name>')[0..8]).
A rule with "opens": true creates accounts that later instructions are checked
against. The program checks every instruction of a call before it runs any, so such
an instruction ends its call and the next one starts after it has run.

common.name: open a token account for the vault (associated, idempotent; the vault pays its own rent)
wrap SOL (transfer into a WSOL account of the vault)
unwrap SOL (close a WSOL account back into the vault)

payout.name: pay out (TransferChecked to a payout wallet only)
